entities.summary:
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, a pivotal event in world history, occurred on June 28, 1914, in Sarajevo, Austria-Hungary. This event sparked a chain reaction that led to the outbreak of World War I, one of the deadliest conflicts in human history.

The archduke, heir to the throne of Austria-Hungary, was shot by Gavrilo Princip, a young Bosnian Serb, while riding in an open car through the Latin Bridge in Sarajevo. The assassination was orchestrated by the Black Hand society, a secret group of Bosnian Serb nationalists who sought to unite Bosnia and Herzegovina with Serbia.

The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand had far-reaching consequences, leading to the outbreak of World War I, which resulted in the deaths of over 37 million people. The war also led to the downfall of four major empires, including the Austro-Hungarian, German, Russian, and Ottoman empires. The war also had a profound impact on international relations and led to the creation of the League of Nations, a precursor to the United Nations.

In the aftermath of the war, the Treaty of Versailles imposed harsh penalties on Germany, contributing to widespread resentment and setting the stage for the rise of Nazi Germany and World War II.
